chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hajjaj al-Khashab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who bequeathed to me wealth, saying, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.' So it was said to her, 'Shall we perform Hajj with it?' She said, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.' So they said to her, 'Shall we give it to the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)?' She said, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah just as she ordered.' I said, 'Order me how I should spend it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let it be spent just as she ordered you. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High is, says: "So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing." Do you see that if she had ordered you to give it to a Jew, would you have given it to a Christian?'

He (the narrator) said: 'So I remained after that for three years, then I came to him and said to him what I had said the first time. So he was silent for a while, then said: 'Give it.' I said, 'To whom shall I give it?' He said: 'Isa Shalqan.'

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Way of Allah (a general term for charitable spending or specific causes)
key_terms.عِيسَى شَلَقَانَ: Isa Shalqan (a specific companion mentioned as the recipient)

ai.seo_question: How should 'in the Way of Allah' be interpreted in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of strict adherence to the testator's specific wording in bequests, using the Quranic verse on altering wills to underscore that 'in the Way of Allah' is not a generic category but a binding instruction. The Imam’s initial silence and subsequent specific naming of Isa Shalqan highlight the scholarly nuance between literal compliance and the Imam’s discretion in identifying the most appropriate recipient within that divine path.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hajaaj Al Khashab,

(The narrator says): ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who bequeathed to me with wealth that I should make it to be in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So it was said to her, ‘We can perform Hajj with it?’ So she said, ‘Make it to be in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So they said to her, ‘Shall we give it to the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>?’ She said, ‘Make it to be in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Make it to be in the Way of Allahazwj just as she had ordered’. I said, ‘Order me how I should make it to be’. Heasws said: ‘Make it to be just as she had ordered you. Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying [2:181] So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing. Do you see that if she had ordered you to give it to a Jew, would you have given it to a Christian?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I remained after that, for three years, then I came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup> similar to what I had said the first time. So he<sup>asws</sup> was silent for a while, then said: ‘Give it’. I said, ‘Whom what I give it to?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Isa Shalqan’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Hajjaj ibn al-Khashshab who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who made a will to spend in the way of Allah. She was asked if it could be spent for al-Hajj. She said, ’Spend it in the way of Allah.’ They asked, ‘Can we give to the family of Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause ?’ She said, ‘Spend it in the way of Allah.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Spend in the way of Allah as you are required.’ I then said, ‘Command me how to spend it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Spend it as she has commanded you. Allah, most Blessed, most High, has said, “Whoever intentionally changes the will of a deceased person, he has committed a sin. Allah is All-hearing and All-knowing.” [2:181] You must consider if she had asked you to give it to a Jew, would you give it to a Christian?’

He (the narrator) has said. ‘I waited thereafter for three years; then I visited him (the Imam) and asked as I had asked him before. He (the Imam) remained quiet for a while, then said, ‘Send it.’ I then asked, ‘To who must I send it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Give it to ‘Isa Shalqan.’”
